system_description: DATU (Decentralized Accountable Trust Union) is a tokenless, offline-capable DAG ledger: signed, hash-chained entries with Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 hybrid signatures, witness checkpoints, identity attestations with a two-signature enrollment ceremony and guardian recovery, and per-record local provenance. Components: Rust node/CLI (datu), HTTP API and explorer, Flutter wallet (Signet vault, phone sign-in), browser SDK, reference relying party, projection indexer. Intended for public-sector record keeping (land titles, registries) and citizen-held identity, globally. Personal data on the ledger is limited to identity statements (keys, labels, claims such as legal name/role) plus whatever payloads operators choose to publish; payloads can be sealed.

approval.rationale: The system is approved for continued development and public deployment as an observer/registry node, conditional on: operators sealing personal fields before publishing; validators running with policy files reviewed per deployment; wire privacy triggers honoured (deploy/operations/wire-privacy.md); revocation and guardian recovery drills kept green in CI.

risk_assessment.assessor: GESF compliance audit + project threat model review
risk_assessment.methodology: NIST RMF + ISO 27005 style walkthrough, documented in .dev-logs/design/production-readiness.md
identified_risks: Ledger data is public by design (personal fields must be sealed); key compromise requires revocation and recovery ceremonies; validator admission policy misconfiguration; wire transport is plaintext TCP today (documented decision with triggers); impostor apps/sites must be countered with attestation and pinning; denial of service on the HTTP surface (bounded by rate limits); regulator obligations for personal claims (GDPR/DPA-PH)
risk_assessment.residual_risk: medium: public-by-default payloads and plaintext transport remain operator decisions documented in deploy/operations/wire-privacy.md
mitigation_measures: Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signatures; append-only revocation as statements; guardian recovery with quorum; sealed fields (deferred delivery supported); HTTP admission limits and per-IP quotas; witness checkpoints and fork evidence; reproducibility
SBOM and signed releases; GESF audit + CI gates

cross_border_transfers: Global by design: the ledger is public and any node may mirror it; operators must assess their own transfers per GDPR Ch. V / DPA-PH
data_inventory.retention_period: Append-only: statements persist while mirrors hold them; erasure is handled by revocation and by not publishing personal payloads (seal instead). Local provenance notes are never synced or served.
